channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Boxing Analyst Predicts Potential Fight Between Janibek Alimkhanuly and Canelo Alvarez
item.description: American boxing analyst Patrick Strumberg has assessed the potential fight between Kazakhstan's Janibek Alimkhanuly and Mexico's Saul 'Canelo' Alvarez. Strumberg believes Alimkhanuly has the technical skill to challenge Alvarez but ultimately favors Alvarez to win, citing his experience and established fighting style.

item.title: Caspian Sea Could Divide Like Aral Sea, Becoming Landlocked, Ecologist Warns
item.description: An ecologist warns that Kazakhstan's northern Caspian Sea may become landlocked by 2100 due to climate change, potentially receding by 3-4 meters by 2050. This could render the area unnavigable and expose the seabed. The Caspian seal's habitat and breeding grounds in this region are particularly threatened, as a lack of ice would impact reproduction. Research is underway to assess the seal's adaptability, though prospects are considered unlikely.

item.title: Contractors to Face Penalties for Delays in Almaty's TEC-3 Modernization
item.description: Samruk-Energy announced that contractors for Almaty's TEC-3 modernization project will face penalties for delays, though the project's cost will not increase. The completion date has been pushed back by a year, with the project only 26% complete as of July. The former chairman of Samruk-Energy was dismissed in October due to unsatisfactory project implementation and lack of oversight on construction deadlines.

item.title: Illegal Gold Mine Discovered in Kazakhstan's Abai Region
item.description: Authorities in Kazakhstan's Abai Region have shut down an illegal gold mining operation. The suspected criminal group extracted over 12,000 cubic meters of ore and damaged more than 4,000 square meters of topsoil. Nine individuals are believed to be involved. A 15-meter deep pit and mining equipment were found at the site.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Energy Ministry Vows to Stabilize Fuel Prices
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Energy will intervene to curb sharp increases in retail prices for AI-92 gasoline and diesel fuel. Minister Yerlan Akkenzhenov assured that sufficient fuel reserves exist, with over 400,000 tons of gasoline and diesel available at depots. He stated there are no conditions for panic buying or price surges.

item.title: Calls for Kyrgyzstan's Emergency Minister to Resign After Teen's Mountain Death
item.description: Social media users in Kyrgyzstan are demanding the resignation of Emergency Situations Minister Kanatbek Chynybaev following the death of 14-year-old Amir Kunakov. The teenager got lost in the Ala-Archa National Park and allegedly did not receive timely rescue assistance. The ministry stated rescue teams were busy with other evacuations when the call was received.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Energy Minister Assures Winter Readiness of Power Plants
item.description: Kazakhstan's thermal power plants are ready for a projected 3% increase in peak load this winter, according to Energy Minister Yerlan Akkenzhenov. He stated that efforts have been made to reduce accidents and improve plant operations. Kazakhstan is nearing full self-sufficiency in electricity and expects a surplus next year.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Energy Minister: No Anticipated Surge in Gasoline Prices
item.description: Kazakhstan does not expect a surge in demand or prices for gasoline, according to Energy Minister Yerlan Akkenzhenov. He stated that fuel reserves are sufficient, with over 400,000 tons of gasoline and diesel available. Factories are operating normally, and distribution is uninterrupted. The minister noted that market conditions and competition influence prices.

item.title: Uzbekistan Considers New Uses for Pasture Lands Beyond Livestock Grazing
item.description: Uzbekistan is reviewing a draft law to diversify the use of pasture lands. Proposals include developing ecotourism, beekeeping, and medicinal plant cultivation alongside traditional livestock grazing. The bill also introduces an electronic platform, 'E-yaylov', for digital pasture management and monitoring using AI and satellite data to prevent land degradation. Public pastures will be established for residents' needs.

item.title: US Renews Travel Warning for Afghanistan, Citing High Security Risks
item.description: The United States has reissued its highest-level travel advisory for Afghanistan, urging citizens not to visit due to severe security risks including terrorism, kidnapping, and crime. The country remains at Level 4, alongside several other nations facing significant threats. The US Embassy in Kabul suspended operations in August 2021.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Parliamentarians Propose Increased Green Space Norms and Protection
item.description: Deputies in Kyrgyzstan's parliament have proposed increasing the green space norm from the drafted 14 m² per person and including neighborhood gardens in protected green areas. The proposals were made during a committee meeting approving a bill to strengthen the protection of green spaces.

item.title: ISIS-Khorasan poses security threat in Afghanistan, exploited by Taliban
item.description: ISIS-Khorasan is a significant security threat in Afghanistan. The Taliban exploits this threat for political and security needs, projecting an image of control domestically while seeking counterterrorism assistance internationally. They also link the ISIS danger to concerns about social media use, potentially for increased digital surveillance.

item.title: Kazakhstan's National Bank to ease bank reserve requirements with digital tenge
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Bank plans to ease mandatory reserve ratio (MRR) requirements for banks by including digital tenge in reserve assets. The digital tenge's share must not exceed 25%. This change aims to enhance regulatory efficiency and includes clarifications on bond classifications and reporting requirements for digital tenge holdings.

item.title: Cricket fans urge completion of stalled stadium in Afghanistan's Maidan Wardak
item.description: Cricket enthusiasts in Afghanistan's Maidan Wardak province are calling for the completion of a stadium construction that began in 2020 and has been unfinished since 2021. Residents believe finishing the stadium would attract players and spectators, boosting local businesses and the sport's development.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Adopts Law to Index Salaries Based on Inflation
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov has signed a law amending the Labor Code of Kyrgyzstan. The new legislation ensures that the real value of employee wages will be maintained through indexation, linked to the rise in consumer prices for goods and services. The procedure for indexation will be determined by collective agreements, except for organizations funded by state budgets.

item.title: Kazakh Prime Minister Orders Special Oversight of Dormitories and Hostels
item.description: Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov has instructed regional administrations and the Ministry of Emergency Situations to extend fire safety month until the end of November. He emphasized the need for special attention to student dormitories, hostels, and educational facilities, noting that many affordable housing options for migrant workers are in poor condition and pose fire risks.

item.title: Kazakhstan Implements Measures to Combat Artificial Border Queues with Uzbekistan
item.description: Kazakh authorities have introduced a new requirement for international cargo carriers at the "Kazyghurt," "B. Konysbayev," and "Atameken" border crossings. Carriers must now deposit a sum equivalent to 20 Monthly Calculation Indices (approximately 86,500 tenge) into a special electronic account to book an electronic queue slot. This measure aims to prevent artificial queue creation and increase carrier responsibility.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Energy System Peak Load to Increase by 3% This Winter, Ministry Projects
item.description: Kazakhstan's energy system peak load is projected to rise by 3% to 18,200 MW during the upcoming heating season. The Ministry of Energy assures that power plants are prepared for maximum consumption, with most repair work completed. Electricity generation has increased by 2.3% year-on-year, and Kazakhstan is nearing self-sufficiency in electricity, expecting a surplus next year.

item.title: KEGOC Production Workers' Average Salary Revealed as 615,000 Tenge
item.description: KEGOC's production workers earn an average monthly salary of 615,000 tenge, according to company chairman Naby Aytzhanov. He stated this at a press conference following a government meeting. Technical staff salaries increase annually by approximately 10%, in line with the Ministry of National Economy's development plans. KEGOC operates the national power grid.

item.title: Kazakhstan Considers Shortening Heating Season Due to Unseasonably Warm Weather
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Energy is monitoring unseasonably warm weather, which may influence the duration of the heating season. Minister Yerlan Akkenzhenov stated that heat supply is regulated based on ambient temperature. Despite mild temperatures in Astana, with no snow in mid-November, energy providers adjust operations to avoid 'heating the air' and aim for efficiency.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Dairy Exports Decline While Honey Shipments Increase
item.description: In January-October 2026, Kyrgyzstan exported 33.5 thousand tons of dairy products, a decrease of 1.1 thousand tons compared to the same period in 2025. Meanwhile, exports of natural honey significantly rose, with shipments reaching 572.41 tons, a 76.3% increase. This comes as 10 Kyrgyz dairy companies received export permits to Russia and Kyrgyz honey gained EU market access.

item.title: Ten HIV-Positive Individuals Sought in West Kazakhstan Region
item.description: Police are searching for ten individuals diagnosed with HIV in the West Kazakhstan region, whose whereabouts are currently unknown. This year, 44 new HIV cases were registered in the region, a decrease from 55 in the same period last year. Currently, 755 people are under dispensary observation, and three HIV-positive individuals have died this year.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Energy Minister Addresses 2027 Gasoline Price Concerns
item.description: Kazakhstan's Minister of Energy, Yerlan Akkenzhenov, commented on expert predictions of gasoline prices reaching 300 tenge per liter by late 2027. He stated that current prices for 92-octane gasoline range from 253-271 tenge, and diesel fuel from 356-367 tenge, attributing the variation to market competition. The minister assured that sufficient fuel reserves and normal production operations prevent any basis for price hikes.

item.title: Germany Condemns Iran-Linked Cyberattacks on French Grocery Stores
item.description: Germany has condemned cyberattacks targeting French grocery stores, which Paris attributes to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). The German Foreign Ministry urged Iran to cease its "destabilizing" activities, calling the attacks unacceptable. The incidents, occurring on October 11-12, affected hundreds of stores, causing refrigeration systems to fail and leading to the spoilage of perishable goods.

item.title: Kazakhstan Minister: Government Will Act on Fuel Price Spikes
item.description: Kazakhstan's Minister of Energy, Akkenzhe Aruak, stated that predicting fuel prices is a "thankless task." However, he assured that in the event of significant price surges, the government will take all necessary measures to stabilize the market and mitigate the impact on consumers.

item.title: France Accuses Iran of Cyberattack on Supermarket Refrigerators
item.description: France has accused Iran of being behind a cyberattack that targeted supermarket refrigerators in October, causing their temperature to rise to 50 degrees Celsius. The incident resulted in losses amounting to tens of millions of euros, impacting operations and potentially causing significant spoilage.

item.title: Junda Oil Refinery Addresses Environmental Concerns Raised by Residents
item.description: The Junda oil refinery has issued an explanation regarding issues raised by residents during a meeting with President Sadyr Japarov. The company emphasized its commitment to environmental safety and stated that a modernization project aimed at reducing environmental impact is in its final stages. Expected reductions in harmful emissions are anticipated upon completion.

item.title: Kazakhstan Approves Capital Market Development Program for 2026-2030
item.description: Kazakhstan has approved a capital market development program for 2026-2030 aimed at enhancing pension asset management and increasing market participation. The program, jointly approved by the Financial Market Development Agency and the National Bank, seeks to provide companies with greater access to long-term financing.

item.title: Kazakhstan Prime Minister Orders Replacement of Aging Gas Cylinders
item.description: Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov has ordered regional authorities to oversee the replacement and withdrawal of aging domestic gas cylinders, citing safety concerns. Approximately 350,000 cylinders are over 40-50 years old. New production facilities are being established, and regulations for cylinder withdrawal and disposal are to be developed within a month.

item.title: Russian Billionaire Boris Rotenberg Involved in $1.5 Billion Dushanbe Construction Project
item.description: Russian billionaire Boris Rotenberg has announced his involvement in the Dushanbe International District, a $1.5 billion multifunctional complex in Tajikistan's capital. The project, developed by TAS International Group, will feature residential buildings, offices, a shopping center, a hotel, and social infrastructure, including a 77-story tower planned to be Central Asia's tallest.

item.title: Iran Rules Out Export of Enriched Uranium Amidst Talks
item.description: Iran's Foreign Ministry has stated that the export of enriched uranium is not on the agenda for current negotiations. Tehran has reportedly shortened its response time to proposals from Washington to demonstrate seriousness. The ministry also noted uncertainty within the US administration regarding negotiation authority and conflicting demands from US officials.

item.title: Closure of 700 Health Centers in Afghanistan Leaves People Stranded Between Illness and No Care
item.description: Over 700 health centers in Afghanistan have closed, raising concerns about access to medical services. Operating centers face shortages of medicine and doctors, impacting low-income families and forcing patients to travel farther for treatment. Citizens urge responsible institutions and aid organizations to find urgent solutions to prevent further suspension of medical services.

item.title: New Irrigation Well Successfully Launched in Kyrgyzstan's Bazar-Korgon District
item.description: A new irrigation well has been successfully test-launched in the Bazar-Korgon district of Kyrgyzstan's Jalal-Abad region, with water now flowing. The Ministry of Agriculture reports that seven new wells are planned for the district to improve water supply for agricultural lands and reduce irrigation water deficit. This follows upgrades to other irrigation systems in the area.

item.title: Tajikistan President Inaugurates New Interior Ministry Lyceum in Dushanbe
item.description: President Emomali Rahmon attended the opening of a new Interior Ministry lyceum, 'Durakhshandagon,' in Dushanbe. The facility includes 28 classrooms, specialized labs, a library, assembly hall, canteen, and a dormitory for 274 students. The lyceum will begin accepting students in 2026, with admissions based on competitive written exams.

item.title: US Democrats Seek to Reinstate Deportation Protections for Afghan Nationals Until 2029
item.description: Democratic lawmakers in the US House are pushing to restore Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for Afghan nationals through July 2029. This effort aims to bypass Republican leadership and force a vote on legislation to protect Afghans facing deportation, amid concerns over Trump administration plans. A federal judge has temporarily blocked proposed deportations.

item.title: Kazakhstan's KazMunayGas Discusses Tengiz and Kashagan Projects with ExxonMobil
item.description: Kazakhstan's national oil company, KazMunayGas, met with representatives from ExxonMobil to discuss the progress of projects at the Tengiz and Kashagan fields. Discussions focused on investment partnerships, geological exploration, oil transportation, and the implementation of modern technologies. Kazakhstan aims to further strengthen its strategic partnership with the American company.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Security Service Uncovers Unaccounted Agricultural Land
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's State Committee for National Security (GKNB) has identified 1,346 hectares of unaccounted agricultural land in the Naryn region. A significant portion of these lands has been used by citizens for over 20 years without lease agreements or rent payments. The GKNB stated that returning these lands to legal circulation will increase local budget revenues and boost agricultural production.

item.title: President Saparov to Attend CSTO Security Council Meeting in Moscow
item.description: Kyrgyz President Saparov will travel to Moscow on November 10-11 to participate in the regular meeting of the Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO) Collective Security Council. The leaders will discuss current international and regional security issues, the CSTO's activities between sessions, and further measures to strengthen collective security. Special attention will be given to combating terrorism and extremism.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Energy Ministry to Adjust Heating Supply Based on Weather Conditions
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Energy will regulate the supply of heat and the temperature of the heat carrier based on weather conditions, according to Minister Erlan Akkenzhe. He stated that energy companies adjust heating supply, but sometimes they "heat the air" due to warm indoor temperatures. The ministry will consider temperature changes during warmer periods to optimize heating delivery.

item.title: Chatham House Award for 2026 Presented to Afghan Women for Resilience
item.description: The UK's Chatham House has awarded its 2026 prize to Afghan women, recognizing their courage and resilience against systematic gender-based persecution. Former UK Prime Minister Theresa May presented the award to Elaheh Safdari, a representative of Afghan women. The award honors their collective resistance and ongoing efforts to advance equality despite severe restrictions.
